mission_04: Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs) extend variational quantum circuits into full machine learning models. A QNN encodes input data into a quantum state via parameterized rotations, processes it through multiple variational layers (each with RY-RZ-RY rotations and entangling CNOTs), and reads out predictions as expectation values of observables. The trainable parameters in the variational layers are optimized classically using gradient descent, with gradients computed via the parameter-shift rule. The Z expectation value on the first qubit provides a binary prediction mapped from [-1, 1] to [0, 1]. In this mission, you implement data encoding, multi-layer variational circuits with entanglement, prediction via observable expectation, binary cross-entropy loss, and gradient-based training using parameter-shift rule.
